title: Human-like moral judgments conceal divergent motive attributions in large language models
abstract: arXiv:2609.07353v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are used to simulate human participants in psychological research. We asked whether LLMs that reproduce human evaluations of a whistleblower's moral character also reproduce the motive attributions that accompany them. Five LLMs and two human samples (N = 125 and N = 742) evaluated a physician who either remained silent about fraudulent billing or reported it to a hospital, regulator, or newspaper. Models reproduced the human ranking of the physician's moral character but portrayed whistleblowers as more helpful, less self-interested, and less hostile. In four of five models, competitive motives were less strongly associated with moral-character judgments. Model ratings changed little when prompts reproduced the narratives and demographic profiles of both human samples, although this comparison cannot isolate a perspective effect. Thus, agreement in average ratings can conceal differences in attributed motive

translated_title: 大语言模型中类人的道德判断掩盖了分化的动机归因
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLMs）被用于在心理学研究中模拟人类被试。我们探讨了那些能够复现人类对举报者道德品格评价的大语言模型，是否也能复现伴随这些评价的动机归因。五个大语言模型和两个人类样本（N = 125 和 N = 742）评估了一位医生，该医生要么对欺诈性收费保持沉默，要么将其举报给医院、监管机构或报纸。模型复现了人类对该医生道德品格的排名，但将举报者描绘得更加乐于助人、更少自私、更少敌意。在五个模型中的四个里，竞争性动机与道德品格判断的关联较弱。当提示词复现了两个人类样本的叙述内容和人口统计特征时，模型评分几乎没有变化，尽管这一比较无法分离视角效应。因此，平均评分上的一致性可能掩盖了归因动机的差异。
tldr: 大语言模型虽能复现人类对举报者的道德品格评价，但其内在的动机归因与人类存在系统性差异，表明平均评分的表面一致可能掩盖深层心理归因的分歧。
